page.layout: One page of text: running head at top centre; below it a heading line with title at left and number XXV at right; then a woodcut engraving in a frame; then a four-line italic verse with large initial L; at the foot the catchword "Circulus" at right. No margin notes.

main_text.head: Pueruli domunculas ex stipulis & assulis construentes. XXV.
main_text.p: [woodcut engraving: children building small houses from straw and chips; not text]

p.i: V dicra ridemus fabricantes tecta puellos, Ex stipulis structum qui meditatur opus: Quid melius plerique agitis, Sanissima Sita Quos huius miseros noxia cura premit?

page.notes: The woodcut shows two women and a man with bricks/blocks and a child-like figure building walls; it is described, not transcribed. The verse opening letter is a large initial L. "Sanissima Sita" and "huius" are read as printed; "Vdicra" is likely "Vdicra" for Vdicra (Iudicra) and should be checked. The line "Quid melius plerique agitis" and "Sanissima Sita" are doubtful and should be checked against the scan.
